main_issue: Whether Agent D may keep wearing her cross tucked in or taped under her clothes, or must take it off entirely for the new no-visible-jewellery rule and tomorrow's manager visit.

A-B.evidence: A says the rule applies to everyone (3); B backs removal (2, 4, 10). At the end A says only not wearing it is sure (24) and B agrees: 'It has to be the same for everyone' (25).

A-C.evidence: C says a check in the morning is enough (13) and that taping works and it's settled (20, 22). A answers 'It's not settled... The only way to be sure is to not wear it' (24).

A-D.evidence: D proposes tucking it in (6) and taping it (16). A rejects both ('I can't risk it' 9; 'Taping it is not the same as taking it off' 24).

B-C.evidence: B says tucking and taping are not the same as removal (10-21). C replies 'You can wear a necklace under your shirt' (11) and 'Let it go' (22).

B-D.evidence: B says D should take it off like B did (19, 21). D argues 'You can't wear earrings under a shirt' (18) and keeps to taping.

C-D.evidence: C backs tucking (11, 13), D agrees 'check it in the morning' (14), and C says 'Taping it works' (20).
